title: Karthigai Deepam Festival
subtitle: Once a year, the silent Hill blazes
meta_description: The Karthigai Deepam festival celebrates Shiva's manifestation as the Tejo-Linga, a boundless pillar of fire. In the Tamil month of Karthigai, Arunachala blazes with the Maha Deepam.
body_html:
Karthigai Deepam at Arunachala

In the sacred Tamil month of Karthigai (mid-November to mid-December), when the full moon aligns with the Krittika star, Arunachala reveals His original form, not as stone nor word, but pure flame. The Karthigai Deepam festival celebrates this timeless manifestation of Lord Shiva as the Tejo-Linga, the boundless pillar of fire.

A festival of light that burns within

Over ten days, the temple town of Tiruvannamalai is transformed. Rituals echo through the corridors of Annamalaiyar Temple, and the divine forms of Shiva and Parvati are carried in procession through the ancient streets. Devotees arrive in the tens of thousands, eyes fixed on the Hill, hearts lit with longing.

The Bharani Deepam: the flame of origin

At dawn on Deepam Day, within the sanctum of the temple, a sacred flame, the Bharani Deepam, is lit. No match or modern fire touches it. Instead, it is kindled through friction, in the ancient way. This is the first spark, the seed of what will come.

The Maha Deepam: Shiva lights the sky

As the sun sets and dusk settles over the Hill, all eyes turn upward. Atop Arunachala's summit, a giant cauldron packed with ghee-soaked wicks is set ablaze. This is the Maha Deepam, the great flame. It burns through the night, visible for miles, still and radiant. In that moment, Arunachala is fire: the hill, the sky, and the heart all alight with Shiva's presence.

Processions, Girivalam, and the town in light

Each evening of the festival, the Pancha Murthis, the five sacred forms of Shiva and Shakti, emerge in procession accompanied by drums, chants, and conches. Devotees walk in rhythm, hands folded, minds silent.

On the night of Deepam, thousands walk the 14-kilometre Girivalam path, barefoot, singing or absorbed in inner stillness. Oil lamps glow in every window, doorstep, and shrine across the town.

The inner meaning of Deepam

The Maha Deepam is no ordinary fire. It is the symbol of the Self, eternal, formless, and luminous. To see it is to be reminded that the light we seek outside already shines within. Every lamp lit during this festival becomes a whisper: "You are That. You are Light."

A living flame through the ages

For centuries, saints like Bhagavan Ramana Maharshi watched the Deepam in silence, their gaze merging with the flame. For the people of Tiruvannamalai and for seekers around the world, this is Arunachala's promise: that even in darkness, the Light never leaves.
